bindings.label: A patient in their 50s presented with recurrent abdominal pain and syncope after drinking alcohol, with symptoms worsening on admission
Symptoms usually occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion and lasted 5-10 minutes; syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
Past medical history included hypertension diagnosed 3 months prior; social history included smoking and alcohol overconsumption (250g/week) for about 20 years
No specific physical examination findings were documented in the case report
ECG shows high-degree AV block, short runs of ventricular tachycardia, and widespread ST-segment elevation
Coronary angiography reveals only mild coronary stenosis
Laboratory tests show normal troponin, potassium, and routine biochemistry, excluding acute myocardial infarction and electrolyte disturbance
Alcohol-induced coronary artery spasm or malignant arrhythmia causing syncope
Alcohol-induced coronary vasospasm causing transient high-degree AV block and ventricular tachycardia
Blood alcohol level was never confirmed
Continuous telemetry monitoring was not performed
Expert analyses identify the ECG/angiography/laboratory pattern as classic for coronary vasospasm
